Below is the full integrated 12‑week program for your 45‑year‑old female client with type 2 diabetes (metformin, HbA1c 7.2%). It combines resistance training, cardio (including supervised fasted mornings), nutrition (calorie deficit, carb timing, protein targets), a weekly cheat meal, an intermittent‑fasting–compatible schedule option, detailed monitoring rules for diabetes, and an intensified Phase 3. Read safety notes before implementation and adapt for any complications or clinician guidance.

Important safety & pre-start checks (must do before starting)
- Obtain medical clearance if she has cardiovascular symptoms, autonomic neuropathy, retinopathy, foot ulcers, severe peripheral neuropathy, or other major comorbidities.
- Explain hypoglycaemia signs (sweating, tremor, confusion, lightheadedness) and have quick carbs (glucose tablets/gel, small juice carton) always available.
- Check capillary BG before first few sessions and while intensifying training. Guidance:
  - If pre-exercise BG <5.0 mmol/L (90 mg/dL): have 10–20 g quick carbs before starting.
  - If 5.0–13.9 mmol/L (90–250 mg/dL): generally safe for low–moderate intensity.
  - If >13.9 mmol/L (250 mg/dL) with ketones: avoid exercise and seek medical advice.
- Foot care and appropriate footwear. Monitor for any neuropathic symptoms.
- Monitor B12 long‑term on metformin; discuss with PCP.

Client targets and nutritional framework
- Calorie target: estimate maintenance then reduce by ~300–500 kcal/day to produce gradual fat loss (~0.25–0.75 kg/week). Adjust after 2 weeks based on weight change.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day (use adjusted body weight if obese).
- Fat: 25–35% of calories, emphasise MUFAs/PUFAs.
- Carbohydrate: remainder of calories; prioritise low-GI carbs, even distribution across meals, carbohydrate periodisation (more on training days).
- Fibre: ≥25–35 g/day.
- Cheat meal: one meal/week (single sitting), preferably after a training session and earlier in the evening, mindful portioning.
- Intermittent fasting: recommended starting approach 14:10 TRE (e.g., 07:00–17:00 or 08:00–18:00). Adjust to 16:8 only if tolerated and monitored.
- Post-workout snacks: 15–30 g protein + 20–40 g carbs depending on intensity (options provided previously).

Monitoring & progression rules
- Weekly weigh-ins; waist measurement every 2 weeks.
- BG: Pre/post exercise for first 2–4 weeks and whenever intensity increases; log episodes.
- Strength progression: increase load 2–5% when target reps achieved for 2 consecutive sessions. Use RPE to autoregulate.
- If weight loss stalls >3 weeks, reduce cheat meal size/frequency or increase NEAT; re-evaluate total calories.
- Reassess at week 12: body measures, 2-week averaged glucose logs, HbA1c with PCP if indicated.

12‑week structure summary
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation & glucose stability
  - Goals: habit building, technique, moderate cardio, introduce fasted cardio (low–moderate) and carb timing.
  - Training: 3 full-body resistance sessions/week (start 2 sets → progress to 3 sets), 2–3 cardio sessions; fasted cardio 2–3 mornings/week (20–25 min easy/moderate walks), steady-state cardio sessions 30–45 min, one short interval introduced in week 3.
  - Nutrition: modest ~300 kcal/day deficit, protein 1.2–1.4 g/kg/day, carb distribution across 3 meals + snack, monitor BG around sessions.

- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength & metabolic acceleration
  - Goals: progressive overload, introduce more interval conditioning, carbohydrate periodisation.
  - Training: Move to heavy/moderate/hypertrophy split across 3 resistance sessions/week:
    - Heavy day (6–8 reps), Moderate (8–12), Hypertrophy (10–15).
    - Intervals 1–2/week (shorter/harder than Phase 1), Saturday longer cardio (45–60 min).
  - Fasted cardio: 3 mornings/week, 25–35 min moderate walks; avoid HIIT fasted.
  - Nutrition: increase protein to 1.3–1.6 g/kg/day, slightly higher carbs on training days, monitor for hypoglycaemia, adjust calories if needed.

- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification & taper for assessment (pushed intensity)
  - Goals: push strength and conditioning intensity, increase metabolic stimulus, then deload for assessment.
  - Training: High-intensity strength (heavy singles/doubles/triples, cluster sets, tempo eccentrics), short heavy metabolic circuits, VO2-style intervals, HIIT (not fasted).
  - Fasted cardio: remain low–moderate; avoid high-intensity fasted efforts.
  - Week 9–11: progressive increases to peak intensity; Week 12: deload with reduced volume (~40% less) and keep some intensity.
  - Nutrition: increase peri-workout carbs around the hardest sessions (30–60 g pre/post as needed), maintain protein 1.3–1.6 g/kg/day, prioritize sleep and recovery, keep weekly cheat meal after training and inside feeding window.

Full week-by-week calendar (detailed; follow each week exactly, adjusting loads per client)

Week 1 (Phase 1 — Establish)
- Monday
  - AM: Fasted cardio — brisk walk 20 min (RPE 3–4). If pre-BG <5.0 mmol/L have 10–15 g carbs.
  - PM: Resistance A — Warm-up 5–8 min bike; Goblet squat 2×10–12; Seated row 2×10–12; DB RDL 2×10–12; Incline push-ups/DB press 2×10–12; Plank 2×30–45 s. Post-workout: 20–30 g protein + 20–30 g carbs.
- Tuesday
  - AM: Fasted cardio — easy bike or walk 20 min (optional).

- Hypoglycaemia risk is lower on metformin than with insulin or sulfonylureas, but exercise (especially fasted cardio) increases glucose uptake and could still precipitate low blood glucose or symptomatic dizziness if calorie intake is too low.

1) Time‑restricted eating (TRE) — 12:12 or 14:10 window

   - 14:10: 14 hours fasting / 10 hours eating (e.g., eat 8:00–18:00). Slightly more aggressive but still gentle.
